notes.24: 26% of candidates chose the correct answer, D. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C, chosen by 51% of candidates. The question asks what can be deduced with certainty. Since both carboxylic acids and alcohols will give steamy fumes with PCl it cannot be deduced with certainty that X is a carboxylic acid, or that it is an alcohol. However, the lack of a visible product with 2,4-DNPH shows that X is definitely not an aldehyde.
notes.27: 25% of candidates chose the correct answer, D. The other three options were each chosen by approximately equal numbers of candidates, suggesting that many had guessed their answer. The question should be approached by counting the OH groups in the product X. Warm dilute H SO will hydrolyse the 2 4 ester link in santonin, producing two OH groups. Cold, acidified KMnO will oxidise the two C=C bonds in santonin, producing four more OH groups. This makes six in total.
notes.33: 34% of candidates chose the correct answer, A. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D, chosen by 41% of candidates. This showed that many candidates did not appreciate that metals have a giant metallic structure, or that ceramics have a giant molecular structure.
notes.34: 15% of candidates chose the correct answer, B. The most commonly chosen incorrect answers were A, chosen by 34%, and C, chosen by 41%. The key to ruling out both A and C is statement 3, ‘X and Y must both be in the same Group of the Periodic Table’. This statement is incorrect, X and Y could be in group 2, or one or both of them could be transition metals.

A possible (and well known) reaction between CH and Cl is the photochemical reaction CH + Cl → CH Cl + HCl. 4 2 4 2 3 The formation of HCl involves the reduction of a chlorine atom from oxidation state 0 to oxidation state -1, therefore the photochemical chlorination of methane is a redox reaction.
notes.general_comments:
This examination paper provided a suitable challenge to the candidates.
Fifteen questions can be said to have been found to be easier. 70% or more of candidates chose the correct
responses to each of Questions 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 13, 17, 18, 22, 23, 30, 32 and 37. Questions 39 and 40

they had sufficient time to complete the paper properly.
Five questions can be said to have been found to be particularly difficult. 35% or fewer candidates chose the
correct responses to each of Questions 24, 27, 33, 34 and 38. Three of these questions were from the
organic sections of the syllabus.
